blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI applied to Property & Casualty. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

P&C economics live in two moments: pricing the risk before the event and handling the claim after it. Both are decision factories — rate against exposure and catastrophe models, settle against policy language and fraud signals — and both reward carriers whose document and data machinery is industrialized.

items: Telematics and GLM pricing outrun validation and filing capacity; model risk documentation is rebuilt under exam.
FNOL, estimates, medical and police files arrive as documents; triage takes days and leakage hides in the queue.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Multimodal AI & Vision-Language Systems, RAG & Enterprise Knowledge Systems, LLM Fine-Tuning & Model Operations from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower, wired into the unit's workflows (FNOL and claims triage, Estimate review and leakage control, Commercial risk surveying) on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — Rate filing regimes among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Voice and avatar interfaces that resolve, not deflect — with emotion-aware escalation and full auditability.
Replace hype with evidence: feasibility, value and adoption risk proven on your data in 6-10 weeks.
Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots.
Repair estimates benchmarked against parts/labor data with anomaly flags (leakage down 15-25%)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: submissions summarized with citations to loss runs, exposure data and appetite rules (quote turnaround down 50% for SME lines). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
